items.title: Three-dimensional radial Carleman inequality with integer weight
items.design_state: local-research-proof-written; exact-hypotheses-retained; not published and not engine-certified
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), in the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $s\ge1$ be an integer and put $\tau=s+1$. Write $r(x)=|x|$ for $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and let $\Delta$ be the Euclidean Laplacian ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Then for every $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$, $$\|r^{-\tau}u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}\le\frac{2}{s}\,\|r^{-\tau+2}\Delta u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}.$$ Moreover, if $u\in H^2(\mathbb R^3)$ is compactly supported in an annulus $\{0<a\le|x|\le b\}$, then the weak second derivatives of $u$ exist as locally square integrable functions, $\Delta u$ denotes their sum in the weak sense ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]), and the same inequality holds for $u$. The weights $r^{-\tau}$ and $r^{-\tau+2}$ are bounded on every fixed compact annulus $\{a_0\le|x|\le b_0\}$ with $0<a_0\le b_0$, and this boundedness on the support of the function is the only property of the weights used in the density extension below; the weight $r^{-\tau}$ is unbounded at the origin for every $s\ge1$, and the weight $r^{-\tau+2}$ is unbounded at the origin for every $s\ge2$ and equals the constant $1$ for $s=1$. That is why the extension is stated for functions whose support stays away from $r=0$. The constant $2/s$ is explicit and is not claimed to be sharp.
items.strategy:
Change of variables. Write $x=rn$ with $r=e^{-t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, $n\in S^2$, and set $u(rn)=r^{-1/2}v(t,n)$, $w(t,n)=e^{st}v(t,n)$. The polar-coordinates formula ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]) and the one-dimensional substitution ([[cor-one-dimensional-change-of-variables-with-absolute-derivative]]) give $dx=r^3\,dt\,d\sigma(n)$, and with $u^2=r^{-1}v^2$ and $\tau-1=s$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}r^{-2\tau}u^2\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}\int_{S^2}w^2\,d\sigma\,dt.$$
The radial computation ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) $\Delta u=r^{-5/2}(\partial_t^2v+\Delta_{S^2}v-\tfrac14v)$ and the substitution $v=e^{-st}w$ give $\partial_t^2v=e^{-st}(\partial_t-s)^2w$; the same factor $e^{2st}$ occurs in $r^{-2\tau+4}(\Delta u)^2r^3\,dt\,d\sigma$, hence
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}r^{-2\tau+4}(\Delta u)^2\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}\int_{S^2}\bigl|\bigl((\partial_t-s)^2+\Delta_{S^2}-\tfrac14\bigr)w\bigr|^2\,d\sigma\,dt.$$
Modal decomposition. Expand $w(t,\cdot)$ for almost every $t$ in the complete orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and use the eigenvalue identity $\Delta_{S^2}Y_{lm}=-l(l+1)Y_{lm}$, a direct computation from the homogeneous extension: $H_l$ is a homogeneous harmonic polynomial and $\Delta=\partial_r^2+2r^{-1}\partial_r+r^{-2}\Delta_{S^2}$ gives $0=r^{-2}(l^2+l+\Delta_{S^2})H_l$. Parseval ([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]) and monotone convergence identify the two displayed integrals with the sums of the modal norms $\sum_{l,m}\|w_{lm}\|^2$ and $\sum_{l,m}\|((\partial_t-s)^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2)w_{lm}\|^2$. Fourier multiplier. In the $2\pi$ convention of [[thm-fourier-differentiation-and-multiplication-identities-on-tempered-distributions]] and Plancherel ([[thm-plancherel]]) the mode operator has symbol $(2\pi i\xi-s)^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2$; with $x=4\pi^2\xi^2\ge0$, $A=s-l-\tfrac12$ and $B=s+l+\tfrac12$, its squared modulus is $(x+A^2)(x+B^2)$, which is increasing in $x\ge0$ and therefore at least $A^2B^2=(s^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2)^2$. For integers $l\ge0$ and $s\ge1$ the integer $l$ minimizing $|s^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2|$ is $l=s-1$ or $l=s$, with value $s-\tfrac14\ge\tfrac s2$, so the squared modulus is at least $s^2/4$. Hence $\|w_{lm}\|\le\tfrac2s\|((\partial_t-s)^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2)w_{lm}\|$ for every mode, and summing the nonnegative squared modal norms gives the inequality for smooth compactly supported $u$. Density extension. On a fixed annulus $a\le r\le b$ the weights $r^{\pm\tau}$, $r^{-\tau+2}$ are bounded. Approximate $u\in H^2(\mathbb R^3)$ with support in that annulus in the $H^2$ norm by $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ functions ([[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]]), multiply each approximant by a smooth cutoff equal to one on a neighbourhood of the support of $u$ and vanishing near the origin ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]); the products lie in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$, still converge to $u$ in $H^2$, and because the weights are bounded on the fixed annulus both sides of the inequality pass to the limit. Countable Choice is declared because it is assumed by [[thm-plancherel]] and by the density corollary; no other choice principle is used.

references.title: D. Tataru, Carleman estimates, unique continuation and applications (Northwestern University, 1998 monograph draft), Chapter 3.6: Theorem 3.50 with Corollary 3.6.1 (singular-weight estimates for the Laplacian) and Theorem 3.52 (strong unique continuation)
S. Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155: Plancherel (Definition 11.22, Theorem 11.29) and the Fourier differentiation identities (Section 12.1)

items.title: Weak unique continuation for bounded potentials in three dimensions
items.design_state: local-research-proof-written; exact-hypotheses-retained; not published and not engine-certified
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be nonempty, open and connected, let
$V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let
$\psi\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ satisfy $\Delta\psi=V\psi$ in the
distributional sense: $\int_\Omega\psi\,\Delta\varphi\,dx=\int_\Omega V\psi\,\varphi\,dx$
for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, with $\Delta\varphi$ the classical
Laplacian. Here $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ denotes the locally integrable
classes on $\Omega$ whose weak derivatives of every order at most two exist
and are locally square integrable
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); $V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$
means that $V$ is measurable and that $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ on every compact
subset, with the essential supremum of
[[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]] and the space of
[[def-l-infinity-on-a-measure-space]]. If $\psi=0$ on a nonempty open subset
of $\Omega$, then $\psi=0$ on $\Omega$. No smoothness, sign, symmetry or decay
hypothesis on $V$ beyond local essential boundedness is used, and no
analyticity is assumed.
items.strategy:
Local propagation step. Let $z\in\Omega$ be a point on a neighbourhood of which $\psi=0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline B_R(z)\subseteq\Omega$; translate the origin to $z$ so that the weight of the Carleman lemma is measured from $z$. Choose $\chi\in C_c^\infty(B_R(0);[0,1])$ with $\chi=1$ on $B_{R/2}(0)$ ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]]) and put $u=\chi\psi$. By the smooth-factor Leibniz rule with $|\alpha|\le2$ ([[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]) $u$ has weak derivatives up to order two in $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$, is compactly supported in $B_R(0)$ and vanishes near $0$; since $\Delta\psi=V\psi$ distributionally, $\Delta u=Vu+e$ with $e=2\nabla\chi\cdot\nabla\psi+(\Delta\chi)\psi$, supported in the annulus $\{R/2\le|x|\le R\}$. Apply the radial Carleman lemma with parameter $s\ge4MR^2$, where $M=\|V\|_\infty$ on $B_R$ ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]): using $r\le R$ on the ball and $|V|\le M$, $\|r^{-\tau}Vu\|\le MR^2\|r^{-\tau}u\|$, and the lemma plus absorption of the term $\tfrac12\|r^{-\tau}u\|$ gives
$$\|r^{-\tau}u\|_2\le\frac4s\|r^{-\tau+2}e\|_2.$$
For $0<\rho<R/2$ one has $u=\psi$ on $B_\rho(0)$ and $r^{-\tau}\ge\rho^{-\tau}$ there, while $e$ is supported where $r\le R$, so
$$\|\psi\|_{L^2(B_\rho(0))}\le\rho^{\tau}\|r^{-\tau}u\|_2\le\frac{4R^2}{s}\Bigl(\frac{2\rho}{R}\Bigr)^{\tau}\|e\|_2\longrightarrow0\qquad(s\to\infty),$$
as $e$ is fixed. Hence $\psi=0$ on $B_{R/2}(z)$: vanishing near a point propagates to the ball of half the radius of any ball around that point that is relatively compact in $\Omega$. Global propagation. Let $Z$ be the union of the open sets on which $\psi$ vanishes; $Z$ is open and nonempty by hypothesis. Fix $x\in\Omega$ and a polygonal path $\gamma:[0,1]\to\Omega$ from a point of $Z$ to $x$, which exists because $\Omega$ is a connected open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-connected-space]], [[cor-components-of-open-subsets-of-rn-are-polygonally-connected]], [[def-polygonal-path-and-polygonal-connectedness]]). The image $\gamma([0,1])$ is compact and disjoint from the closed set $\mathbb R^3\setminus\Omega$, so it has distance $\delta>0$ from it ([[lem-relative-compact-closed-sets-have-a-positive-distance-gap]]). By uniform continuity of $\gamma$ on $[0,1]$ choose $0=t_0<\dots<t_N=1$ with $|\gamma(t_{j+1})-\gamma(t_j)|<\delta/4$. Inductively, if $\psi=0$ near $\gamma(t_j)$, then $B_{\delta/2}(\gamma(t_j))$ has closure in $\Omega$, so the propagation step with $R=\delta/2$ gives $\psi=0$ on $B_{\delta/4}(\gamma(t_j))$, a neighbourhood of $\gamma(t_{j+1})$; hence $\psi=0$ near $x=\gamma(t_N)$. As $x\in\Omega$ was arbitrary, $Z=\Omega$. Consequently $\Omega\setminus Z$, which is open in $\Omega$, is empty: otherwise $Z,\Omega\setminus Z$ would be a separation of $\Omega$ ([[def-connected-space]]). This proves $\psi=0$ on $\Omega$. Countable Choice is inherited through the Carleman lemma; no further choice principle is used.

references.title: B. Davey, Quantitative unique continuation for the Laplacian plus a potential (arXiv:1903.04021)
D. Tataru, Carleman estimates, unique continuation and applications (Northwestern University monograph, 1998)

items.title: Exterior spherical multipole expansion and the ball boundary series
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ vanish outside $\overline B_a(0)$. Use the complete orthonormal basis $\{Y_{lm}\}$ of real spherical harmonics on $S^2$ with unnormalised surface measure $d\sigma$ of total mass $4\pi$ and the addition theorem of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]], and the Legendre generating kernel and its compact remainder bound from [[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]. Write $x=rn$, $r=|x|$, $n\in S^2$. Then:

(a) **Exterior multipole expansion.** For every $x$ with $|x|>a$, $$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y)}{|x-y|}\,dy=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^lY_{lm}(y/|y|)\rho(y)\,dy,$$ the series converging absolutely and uniformly on $\{|x|\ge r_0\}$ for every $r_0>a$, with tail after degree $N$ bounded by $\|\rho\|_1\,a^{N+1}/(r_0^{N+2}(1-a/r_0))$; for every fixed $r>a$, the degree-$l$ term is the $L^2(S^2,d\sigma)$ angular projection of $n\mapsto F_r(n):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|rn-y|^{-1}\rho(y)\,dy$ onto the degree-$l$ harmonics. This function is continuous and bounded by $\|\rho\|_1/(r-a)$, so it is in $L^2(S^2)$; no sphere trace or $L^2$ property of the volume density $\rho$ is asserted. The degree-zero and degree-one terms are the Coulomb and dipole terms with the explicit remainder bound of [[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]] ($Q=\int\rho$, $p=\int y\rho(y)\,dy$, $|R(x)|\le16a^2\|\rho\|_1/|x|^3$ for $|x|\ge2a$).

(b) **Termwise differentiation.** On every compact $K$ with $\inf_K|x|>a$ the series may be differentiated termwise to every order, the differentiated series converging uniformly on $K$; in particular the potential is $C^\infty$ on $\{|x|>a\}$.

(c) **Ball boundary branch.** For $f\in L^2(S^2)$ with coefficients $f_{lm}$ the series $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}r^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n)$ converges in $L^2(S^2)$ as $r\uparrow1$ and, with all derivatives, uniformly on each closed ball of radius $<1$, is harmonic on the open unit ball, and is the unique harmonic function there with a finite $\sup_{r<1}\|u(r\cdot)\|_2$ and $L^2$ boundary limit $f$; for continuous $f$ it equals the Poisson integral $(1-r^2)/(4\pi|rn-n'|^3)$ of $f$ and extends continuously to the closed ball with boundary values $f$.

This is a statement about the Newtonian integral of a compactly supported $L^1$ density and about harmonic functions; no physical charge distribution or electrostatic interpretation is asserted. In every coefficient integral the factor $|y|^lY_{lm}(y/|y|)$ is defined at $y=0$ by its homogeneous polynomial extension: zero for $l\ge1$ and the constant degree-zero harmonic for $l=0$. This is a finite assignment, and changing its value at that null singleton changes no integral.
items.strategy: Assembly of the recorded branches. Write $q=|y|/r$ and $z=n\cdot y/|y|$ for $y\ne0$; the convergent Legendre kernel [[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]] gives $|x-y|^{-1}=\sum_l(|y|^l/r^{l+1})P_l(z)$ for $|y|\le a<r$, with the stated geometric tail, and integration against the finite measure $\rho\,dy$ yields the zonal multipole series with the displayed error times $\|\rho\|_1$. Substituting the addition theorem $P_l(z)=\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\sum_mY_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(y/|y|)$ from [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]] into the $l$-th term and separating variables gives the displayed spherical-harmonic coefficients, the finite sums agreeing with the zonal series for every degree, hence in the uniform limit. The degree-zero and degree-one coefficients are $Q$ and the components of $p$, and comparison with the explicit Coulomb-dipole splitting of [[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]] (twice the fundamental theorem applied to $h(s)=|x-sy|^{-1}$) identifies the remainder and its bound. For the projection assertion fix r>a. Uniform convergence of the degree series on the observation sphere and the finite sphere measure allow its inner product with each Y_km to be taken termwise. Orthogonality gives $\langle F_r,Y_{lm}\rangle=(4\pi/(2l+1))r^{-l-1}q_{lm}$, proving exactly the stated angular projection, not a nonexistent restriction of rho to a sphere. Absolute convergence of the full double series follows from $\sum_m|Y_{lm}(n)q_{lm}|\le\int|y|^l|\rho(y)|\sum_m|Y_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(y/|y|)|dy\le((2l+1)/(4\pi))a^l\|\rho\|_1$ by finite Cauchy-Schwarz and the addition diagonal identity. The same geometric series yields the stated degree tail. For (b), the corrected kernel lemma supplies harmonicity of every coefficient term and uniform kernel/source tail on a bounded slightly larger exterior neighbourhood Kplus of K. Apply [[thm-interior-derivative-estimates-for-harmonic-functions]] to harmonic partial-sum differences on fixed-radius balls inside Kplus: their every-derivative suprema on K are bounded by fixed constants times the already vanishing uniform tail bound on Kplus. Finite-coordinate FTC [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]] identifies the uniform derivative limits with the derivatives of the Newton integral. This proves the full every-order compact convergence using the exact real harmonic estimate, with no Cauchy estimate or unprovided complex-parameter domain. For (c), the addition theorem gives $\sum_m|Y_{lm}(n)|^2=(2l+1)/4\pi$, so Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the absolute tail at fixed $r<1$ by $\|f\|_2(\sum_{l>N}r^{2l}(2l+1)/4\pi)^{1/2}\to0$; the derivative estimates and the interior harmonic estimates of [[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]] give uniform convergence of all derivatives on smaller balls, orthogonality gives $\|u(r\cdot)-f\|_2\to0$, and the corrected radius-s Poisson representation followed by harmonic orthogonality gives $v_{lm}(r)=(r/s)^l v_{lm}(s)$; the L2 boundary limit fixes the coefficient and proves uniqueness in the stated class; the Poisson kernel identity and uniform boundary convergence for continuous $f$ are the last part of that lemma. Completeness and orthonormality of the basis are those of [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]. In the ball clause the L2 trace, finite radial L2 bound, uniqueness and continuous-data Poisson representation are the exact corrected H3 branches; their Countable Choice assumption is retained. No ball boundary assertion is inferred for rho at radius a.

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis)

S. Axler, P. Bourdon, W. Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed. (Springer GTM 137), author-hosted full text, Chapter 5 (harmonic polynomials, spherical harmonics and zonal harmonics) and Chapter 1 (Poisson kernel for the ball)

items.title: Well-posed weak solvability and classical regularity for declared smooth-domain elliptic boundary problems
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the weak-solvability and regularity lemmas below ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the local graph sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive, that is $\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le eta|\xi|^2$ for all $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ and $x\in\Omega$ and some $0<\alpha\le eta<\infty$, and let $ho$ be smooth on $\overline\Omega$. The Euclidean inner product is that of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; at a boundary point with outward unit normal $
u$ the outward conormal vector is $\varepsilon
u$ and the outward conormal derivative is $
u\cdot\varepsilon
abla u$. Here $\operatorname{Sym}^3$ is the space of real symmetric $3	imes3$ matrices, $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ is the Sobolev space of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], $H_0^1(\Omega)$ is the $H^1$ closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]), and $T:H^1(\Omega)	o H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ is the bounded onto trace of [[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]], with the fractional boundary space defined in [L1]. Then:

(a) **Dirichlet.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one weak solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u\,dx=\int_\Omegaho v\,dx$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$; it depends continuously on the data, $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|ho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$, has a $C^\infty$ representative on $\overline\Omega$, and satisfies the classical equations $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ in $\Omega$ and $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$.

(b) **Neumann.** Let $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ be a smooth outward conormal datum satisfying $\int_{\Omega_j}ho\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g\,dS=0$ on every connected component $\Omega_j$ of $\Omega$. Then there is a weak solution of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$; it is unique up to a separately chosen additive constant on each component, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ on every component gives a unique normalised solution which is $C^\infty$ on each closed component and satisfies the classical equations $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ in $\Omega$ and $
u\cdot\varepsilon
abla u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$. In particular on a connected domain the compatibility is $\int_{\partial\Omega}g=-\int_\Omegaho$, with a single additive constant.

(c) **Transmission.** Let there be finitely many pairwise disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, let $\varepsilon$ be piecewise smooth on the closures of the resulting pieces and uniformly positive in the above sense, let $ho$ be piecewise smooth on the closed pieces and let $\sigma$ be a smooth sheet charge on the union of the interfaces; the weak right-hand side is $\int_\Omegaho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$, together with $\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ in the Neumann case. Prescribe either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum of (a), or the smooth outer Neumann datum of (b) with the componentwise compatibility condition $\int_{\Omega_j}ho+\sum_{\Gamma\subset\Omega_j}\int_\Gamma\sigma+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$ for every component $\Omega_j$. With outer Dirichlet data the globally $H^1$ solution is unique; with outer Neumann data it exists exactly when that compatibility holds and is then unique modulo componentwise additive constants, the zero componentwise means making it unique; the equal one-sided traces and $C^\infty$ regularity on each closed side hold in either case, and the flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ in the sign convention of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], where $n$ is a chosen unit normal on the interface and $[\varepsilon
abla u]=\varepsilon^+
abla u^+-\varepsilon^-
abla u^-$ is the difference from the $n$-positive side to the other.

Edge and junction points, reentrant corners, coefficient loss of regularity and general piecewise classical regularity beyond finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces are excluded. The existence content of all three parts is that of the two weak solvability lemmas; this theorem states the combined existence-and-regularity conclusions on the declared domains and adds no existence assertion beyond them.
items.strategy: The claim collects three recorded branches and their compatibility. (a) Existence, uniqueness, exact prescribed trace and continuous dependence are [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]; the classical upgrade to $C^\infty$ on the closure, with the classical equation and boundary values, is [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (b) Testing the displayed weak identity with the constant on each component gives $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$, including the minus sign when solved for the outer conormal integral. Necessity of componentwise compatibility, existence, uniqueness modulo componentwise constants and the normalised form are [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; the classical upgrade is again [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (c) Apply the transmission functional including the sheet-charge term, with outer Dirichlet tests in $H_0^1$ for full uniqueness, or outer Neumann tests in $H^1$ with that functional zero on every componentwise constant and the chosen mean normalisation. The weak existence and the one-sided trace identity are the transmission part of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], the two-sided classical smoothness and the jump relation are [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]], and the passage from the weak identity to the interface flux uses the divergence theorem for the piecewise smooth configuration together with the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. The smooth coefficients, conormal field and chart changes are smooth by the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]; the inner products and the quadratic form $\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u$ use the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No existence or regularity claim is made beyond the stated smooth-domain, finite-interface regime.

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis)

items.title: Uniqueness of the outgoing scalar Helmholtz solution with a smooth obstacle
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the modal DtN/trace suppliers, covering the Countable Choice used by the local UCP supplier. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) whose exterior $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ is connected, let $k>0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$. Suppose $u$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ on $D$ with the Euclidean Laplacian $\Delta$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), vanishes on $\partial O$, and is outgoing in the class of [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: its trace $f=u|_{S_R}$ lies in $H^{1/2}(S_R)$ and its normal derivative on $S_R$ is $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense of that lemma. Then $u=0$ on $D$. No decay rate, asymptotic expansion or pointwise Sommerfeld formula beyond the stated outgoing class is assumed.
items.strategy: Green's identity on the truncated exterior. Apply the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] to $u$ and its complex conjugate on the bounded $C^1$ domain $D\cap B_R$, whose boundary consists of $\partial O$ and $S_R$: the volume integral is the real number $\int_{D\cap B_R}(|\nabla u|^2-k^2|u|^2)\,dx$, and the inner boundary contributes zero because $u=0$ on $\partial O$. The full boundary pairing equals that real volume integral, so its imaginary part is zero; its real part need not vanish. Thus $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=0$. By [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]] applied to $f$ the imaginary part is $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2$ with $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$; the already established zero imaginary pairing and the strictly positive modal coefficients force every $f_{lm}=0$. Consequently the outgoing exterior series of that lemma, which is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$, vanishes on $\{r>R\}$; combined with $u=0$ on $\partial O$ the function $u$ vanishes on the complement of $D\cap\overline B_R$. Propagation. On $D$ the real and imaginary parts of $u$ are $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ solutions of $\Delta w=Vw$ with the bounded coefficient $V=-k^2$, so [[thm-bounded-potential-weak-unique-continuation-in-three-dimensions]] applies to each of them on the connected open $D$: each vanishes on the nonempty open set $D\cap\{r>R\}$, hence on $D$. Therefore $u=0$ on $D$. No finite experimental observation or physical postulate is used.

TU Dortmund, Lecture notes: The Rellich Lemma on the Helmholtz equation

items.title: Existence and uniqueness for the smooth exterior vector Helmholtz mixed boundary problem
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, as used by the variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers and by the Fredholm alternative ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) whose exterior $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ is connected, let $k>0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$. Write $A:=B_R(0)\setminus\overline O$ and let $n$ be the outward unit normal field of $A$, so that on $\partial O$ the field $n$ points into $O$; extend $n$ to a smooth normal collar by $n(p+sn(p)):=n(p)$, so $\partial_n n=0$, using [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]; put $\kappa:=\operatorname{div}n|_{\partial O}$ and, for a field $E$ on $\partial O$, $E_n:=E\cdot n|_{\partial O}$.

For $e_T:\partial O\to\mathbb C^3$ smooth in boundary charts and satisfying $e_T\cdot n=0$, put
$$\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T:=\operatorname{div}\widetilde e_T-\partial_n(\widetilde e_T\cdot n)\quad\text{on }\partial O,$$
where $\widetilde e_T$ is any smooth extension of $e_T$ to a neighbourhood of $\partial O$; the expression is independent of the extension and equals the surface divergence of $e_T$ with respect to the Euclidean surface measure of $\partial O$. Write $\Delta$ for the Euclidean Laplacian ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), acting componentwise, and for a vector field $f=(f_1,f_2,f_3)$ on $S_R$ write $T_Rf:=(T_Rf_1,T_Rf_2,T_Rf_3)$ with $T_R$ the scalar Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]].

Then there is exactly one field $E\in C^\infty(\overline D;\mathbb C^3)$ with
$$(\Delta+k^2)E=0\ \text{on }D,\qquad \operatorname{div}E=0\ \text{on }D,\qquad E_{\text{tangential}}=e_T\ \text{on }\partial O,$$
which is outgoing on the sphere $S_R$ in the modal sense of that lemma: its trace $f:=E|_{S_R}$ lies in $H^{1/2}(S_R;\mathbb C^3)$ and the normal derivative of $E$ on $S_R$ equals $T_Rf$ componentwise in the weak trace sense of the sphere DtN lemma. With these data the normal boundary values of $E$ on $\partial O$ satisfy the closure relation
$$\partial_nE_n+(\operatorname{div}n)E_n=-\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$$
as an identity of $C^\infty$ functions on $\partial O$. No scalar Dirichlet condition is imposed on the three Cartesian components of $E$, and no decay rate, asymptotic expansion or pointwise Sommerfeld formula beyond the stated modal outgoing class is assumed.
items.strategy:
Reduction to a coercive shifted form. On the truncated annulus $A=B_R\setminus\overline O$ introduce $X=\{v\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3):v_{	ext{tangential}}=0	ext{ on }\partial O\}$, a closed subspace of $H^1$ by the trace continuity of [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]; the trace machinery is smooth for the classical solutions. With $\kappa=\operatorname{div}n$ on the inner boundary, the form
$$a(E,v)=\int_A igl(
abla E:\overline{
abla v}-k^2E\cdot\overline v igr)+\int_{\partial O}\kappa E_n\overline{v_n}-\langle T_RE,vangle_{S_R}$$
is bounded on $H^1$ by [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]] and bounded $\kappa$. Its real part is coercive after shifting by a real $\lambda>k^2+C_\delta+1$: the outer term is nonnegative by the sign of $\operatorname{Re}T_R$, and the curvature term is absorbed by the collar inequality proved in [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] with $2ab\le\delta a^2+\delta^{-1}b^2$. The complex coercive form is inverted by the explicit contraction iteration (Hilbert Riesz representation [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]] turns the shifted form into a bounded operator $B$ with $\operatorname{Re}\langle Bx,xangle\ge\alpha\|x\|^2$; for small $t>0$, $x\mapsto(I-tB)x+tf$ is a strict contraction in the complete space). The $L^2$ pairing $J:X	o X^*$ is compact because the argument of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] gives $X\hookrightarrow L^2$ compact on the smooth bounded domain $A$; the original form operator is a shifted inverse composed with $I-\lambda K$, $K$ compact, so the Fredholm alternative [[thm-fredholm-alternative-for-identity-minus-compact]] (with its Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) gives bounded invertibility once the kernel is zero. Kernel. For a homogeneous solution the imaginary part of $a(E,E)$ is $-\operatorname{Im}\langle T_RE,Eangle=0$, and the strictly positive DtN imaginary coefficients force all three outer traces of $E$ to vanish. Extending the field by the outgoing series outside $B_R$ and integrating by parts with [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] gives a weak componentwise Helmholtz solution on $D$ with $H^1$ regularity on each bounded local patch, because the full traces agree across $S_R$, and it vanishes outside $B_R$. On each such patch apply [[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]] with principal matrix $I$, $b=0$, $c=-k^2$, $f=0$ (equivalently $-\Delta E=k^2E$), giving $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$. The real and imaginary parts of each component then satisfy $\Delta w=-k^2w$ on the connected $D$ and vanish on its nonempty exterior open subset, so the direct local supplier [[thm-bounded-potential-weak-unique-continuation-in-three-dimensions]] makes them zero. No scalar inner Dirichlet condition is inferred from tangential PEC data, and the scalar exterior-Dirichlet lemma is not invoked in this kernel step. Hence the kernel is zero and the shifted-then-unshifted problem is boundedly invertible. Inhomogeneous data. For prescribed smooth $e_T$, give each Cartesian scalar component the Dirichlet boundary datum $(e_T)_j$ on $\partial O$ and zero on $S_R$. The weak prescribed-trace solver [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]] with principal coefficient $I$ and zero bulk source, followed by the scalar smooth-data upgrade [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]], supplies a smooth componentwise lift $G$ on $\overline A$ with $G|_{\partial O}=e_T$ and $G|_{S_R}=0$ (apply to real and imaginary parts). This is a genuine scalar use of B7, distinct from the inline vector mixed-boundary regularity proof. Now solve for $u\in X$ with $a(u,v)=-a(G,v)-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}$; $E=G+u$ then has the prescribed tangential trace, and testing against compactly supported interior fields gives the componentwise Helmholtz equation and the stated normal relation. Regularity. At the artificial sphere the matched traces and normal derivatives make the extended field a weak Helmholtz solution across $S_R$, so [[cor-smooth-data-give-smooth-interior-solutions]] applied on bounded local patches to the constant-coefficient operator $-\Delta-k^2$ makes the matched field smooth there; no boundary theorem is used at this artificial interior surface. At $\partial O$ rotate into a smooth frame with two tangential components and one normal component; the principal part becomes a uniformly elliptic scalar principal matrix times the identity with smooth lower-order coupling, and the boundary system (two Dirichlet components and one Robin component) is complementing: in the frozen half-space a decaying principal mode $e^{i\xi\cdot y-|\xi|t}a$ with $\xi
e0$ has $a_1=a_2=0$ and $-|\xi|a_3=0$, so all amplitudes vanish, while curvature and connection terms are lower order. Supply the vector boundary argument inline, rather than treating B7's scalar public statement as a vector theorem. After the smooth frame rotation and boundary flattening, tangential shifts preserve the two zero Dirichlet component traces, while the normal component has arbitrary admissible trace. Test with $-\delta_{-h}(\eta^2\delta_h u)$ componentwise. The scalar principal matrix times the identity gives the sum of three positive gradient squares; smooth coefficient and frame commutators are lower-order $L^2$ terms bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz and Young. The differenced Robin boundary term consists of the bounded Robin coefficient times the normal quotient trace square and its smooth coefficient commutator; the collar estimate $\|w\|_{L^2(\partial O)}^2\le\delta\|
abla w\|_2^2+C_\delta\|w\|_2^2$ absorbs the first term, and trace continuity and Young bound the commutator by the same gradient bound and known $H^1$ data. This gives uniform tangential quotient-gradient bounds. Riesz identifies all mixed second derivatives in $L^2$, and the corrected component equation recovers each normal second derivative using the uniformly positive normal principal coefficient. Iterate the tangential quotient argument with differentiated smooth data and coefficient/Robin commutators, and recover remaining normal orders from the component equations; a finite boundary cover gives all orders. Local Sobolev extension/embedding then gives classical smooth representatives. This is the actual inline mixed-boundary product-space proof obligation, with two Dirichlet components and one Robin component; it is not replaced by a scalar Dirichlet-regularity citation. Divergence. The scalar $q=\operatorname{div}E$ is a smooth Helmholtz solution on $D$; the divergence identity in a boundary frame turns the inner Robin relation into $q=0$ on $\partial O$, and the outgoing component series differentiates to an outgoing $q$; [[lem-em-exterior-outgoing-scalar-uniqueness]] then gives $q=0$ on $D$. Thus $\operatorname{div}E=0$ is deduced, not presumed.

items.title: Spectral completeness of the declared PEC waveguide and cavity classes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the local graph sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], with outward Euclidean unit normal field $\nu$ on $\partial\Omega$. Restate the class conventions of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: $L^2:=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ is the real Hilbert space of square integrable vector fields with the inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=\int_\Omega u\cdot v\,dx$ induced by the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and
$$H(\operatorname{curl})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{curl}u\in L^2\},\qquad H(\operatorname{div})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{div}u\in L^2\}$$
are the graph spaces with norms $\|u\|^2_{H(\operatorname{curl})}=\|u\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_2^2$ and $\|u\|^2_{H(\operatorname{div})}=\|u\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}u\|_2^2$, the curl and divergence being taken in the distributional sense; $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the fields that are smooth on a neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$ and satisfy $\nu\times u=0$ pointwise on $\partial\Omega$; and $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$, $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. This is the explicit weak perfect-electric-conductor class of that item, not an identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation.

Then:

(a) **Smooth PEC cavity.** The curl form $(u,v)\mapsto\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v$ on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, with $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional and with the finite-dimensional zero eigenspace retained. Each eigenfield $u_j\in V$ satisfies $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally together with the PEC trace; and $u_j$ has a $C^\infty$ representative on $\overline\Omega$ for which $\operatorname{div}u_j=0$, $\nu\times u_j=0$ and $\partial_\nu u_{j,n}+(\operatorname{div}\nu)u_{j,n}=0$ hold classically on $\partial\Omega$, where $u_{j,n}=u_j\cdot\nu$ and $\nu$ is extended constant along collar normal lines. For every explicitly chosen positive mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and every pair of data $q_0\in V$, $q_1\in H$, the associated second-order wave has coefficients solving $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with $a_j(0)=\langle q_0,u_j\rangle$ and $a_j'(0)=\langle q_1,u_j\rangle$, in the modal class of that item: its displacement lies in $C(\mathbb R;V)$ and its velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$, finite modal sums converge in $C(K;V)$ and $C(K;H)$ on every compact time interval $K$, and the finitely many $\lambda_j=0$ modes are $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The speed is a positive abstract mathematical parameter and has no physical dependency. The scalar auxiliary Dirichlet resolvent used inside the recorded cavity argument has, for every $q\in L^2(\Omega)$, a unique solution $\varphi\in H_0^1(\Omega)\cap H^2(\Omega)$ of $(1-\Delta)\varphi=q$, with smooth zero-boundary approximants converging in $H^2$ and whose gradients converge in the PEC graph norm, by [[lem-em-dirichlet-resolvent-h-two-and-smooth-test-density]]. For smooth $q$ this solution is smooth on the closure by the same smooth-boundary bootstrap; no classical regularity for a general $L^2$ datum is asserted. Smooth unshifted scalar boundary problems have the classical upgrade of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] with $\varepsilon=I$.

(b) **Rectangular reflection-parity class.** Let $Q=\prod_{j=1}^3(0,L_j)$ with $L_j>0$ and let $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ be constants. In the reflection boundary class of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (real $L^2$ fields on the torus $\prod_j\mathbb R/(2L_j\mathbb Z)$ whose components carry the parities of that item and whose distributional divergences vanish), the finite separated Fourier modes are dense at every time, and every initial datum of the class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class, along which $\tfrac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)\,dx$ is constant.

No completeness is asserted in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes, and the constant-Ohmic and open-longitudinal branches are homed separately as physical items on the guide page; they are not mathematical premises or dependencies of this statement.
items.strategy: The smooth-cavity spectral and finite-energy assertions are exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: its shifted coercive full-$X$ solution operator, divergence projection using the proved scalar Dirichlet resolvent and smooth-zero-boundary density, and compact self-adjoint spectral theorem give the complete $H^1$ graph-class eigenbasis, multiplicities, distributional equations and modal wave expansion with topology zero modes retained, for the explicitly quantified $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and arbitrary $V\times H$ data. The source distinguishes displacement $C(\mathbb R;V)$ from velocity $C(\mathbb R;H)$ with uniform convergence on compact time intervals; no unquantified physical speed is used. Each eigenfield satisfies its full-$X$ variational identity, so [[lem-em-pec-cavity-eigenfield-boundary-regularity]] gives the promised $C^\infty$ eigenfields on the closure, including $\lambda=0$. That supplier proves the coupled vector mixed boundary estimate and admissible tests in the chosen completion; the scalar [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] is used only for its actual scalar auxiliary boundary solvability and is not treated as a vector PEC regularity theorem. The quadratic graph forms and curl/div expressions use [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No classical smoothness of general finite-energy sums follows or is asserted. The rectangular assertions are unchanged [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (G2): reflection parities give the rectangular torus class; trigonometric product completeness and the finite-dimensional Fourier ODE conserve $\varepsilon|\hat E|^2+|\hat B|^2/\mu$, yielding the unique weak energy solution. The direct TE/TM verification G1 remains a physical branch on the guide page. The approved K10 constant-Ohmic and open-longitudinal branches are now explicitly homed there as pthm-em-uniform-ohmic-modal-decay and pthm-em-open-rectangular-guide-completeness. These are subject-homing records, not mathematical premises or dependencies of this pure mathematical wrapper.

items.title: Explicit mathematical hypothesis/convention examples
items.statement:
**Spatial coordinate convention.** Throughout this example, the local spatial labels $i=1,2,3$ name the canonical function coordinates $i-1\in\{0,1,2\}$: $x_i:=x(i-1)$ and $n_i:=n(i-1)$. The local vector $e_i$ is defined by $e_i(k)=1$ when $k=i-1$ and $e_i(k)=0$ otherwise, for $k<3$. Likewise, $\partial_i$ denotes differentiation in canonical coordinate $i-1$, and every spatial vector component with label $i$, including $g_i$, follows this same convention. A printed triple lists these components in the order $i=1,2,3$. This finite relabelling does not permute the coordinate order, change the Euclidean gradient, divergence or curl, or change the dimension subscripts in $\mathbb R^3$, $\lambda_3$ and $S^2$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]).

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Three exact boundary checks. (i) The sphere trace $f(n)=n_3$ is the trace of the homogeneous degree-one harmonic polynomial $u(x)=x_3$, so the ball boundary branch of [[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]] applies to it; the simultaneous conditions $\Delta u=0$ in the unit ball $B_1$ and $\partial_nu=1$ on $S^2$ are incompatible, because the divergence theorem gives $0=\int_{B_1}\Delta u\,dx=\int_{S^2}\partial_nu\,d\sigma=\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$. (ii) For the coefficient $\varepsilon=1$ on $\{x_1<0\}$ and $\varepsilon=2$ on $\{x_1>0\}$, the function $u=x_1$ on the first side and $u=x_1/2$ on the second is continuous and has weak first derivatives represented by locally integrable functions, and $\varepsilon\partial_1u\equiv1$, so $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=0$ weakly although $u$ is not $C^1$: its first derivative jumps from $1$ to $1/2$ across the interface. Hence the smooth-coefficient statements of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] cannot be extended to this piecewise-constant case, and the correct conclusion there is the piecewise regularity recorded by that item, not a global $C^1$ or $C^\infty$-on-the-closure statement. (iii) The same coefficient configuration is a hypothesis boundary for the smooth-domain spectral completeness of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]]: the coefficient field is discontinuous across the interface and the explicit weak solution is not classical $C^1$ there, so the configuration lies outside the smooth classes of that theorem, which asserts no completeness or classical boundary regularity in non-smooth classes; the weak formulation nevertheless remains valid. All three parts are exact finite computations or classical divergence-theorem evaluations, and they assert no physical interpretation.
items.strategy:
Direct computations. Part (i): $\Delta x_3=0$ and $
abla x_3=e_3$, so on the unit sphere $\partial_nx_3=e_3\cdot n=n_3$; if a function were harmonic in $B_1$ with $\partial_nu=1$ on $S^2$, the divergence theorem [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to $
abla u$ (a $C^1$ field) would give $0=\int_{B_1}\Delta u\,d\lambda=\int_{S^2}\partial_nu\,d\sigma$, while the polar-coordinates formula [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] and the defining normalisation give $\sigma(S^2)=3\lambda_3(B_1)=4\pi$; the contradiction $0=4\pi$ proves incompatibility, and the Laplacian is that of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. Part (ii): on each open half-space the field $\varepsilon
abla u$ is the constant $(1,0,0)$, so its distributional divergence is zero ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]): testing $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)$ against a compactly supported smooth test function and integrating by parts reduces to $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\partial_1\varphi\cdot(-1)\,dx=0$ for a constant field. The function $u$ is continuous because $x_1$ and $x_1/2$ both tend to $0$ at the interface, its distributional first derivatives are the locally integrable functions equal to $1,0,0$ respectively $1/2,0,0$ on the two sides ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]), and these representatives jump at $x_1=0$, so $u$ is $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but not $C^1$. Part (iii): this is the statement that the excluded case is excluded: the smooth coefficients and smooth interfaces required by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] and by the smooth-domain class of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] fail, while the displayed weak solution exists and is not smooth on the closure. No physical postulate, measurement or empirical claim is used. Countable Choice is inherited by the actually used Green, surface/regular-distribution and/or harmonic-boundary supplier interfaces. The supplier updates do not alter the local source, trace or modal class used here.
